sources.title: How To Apply for NC Medicaid (NC DHHS)
sources.supports: Claim-verification note (HACK-17): page retrieved 2026-10-30; the page displays 'last modified 10/08/2026'. Verified on this page: the four application channels (online ePASS, in person at a local DSS, by phone, by mail/email/fax/drop-off); the 'apply at any time of the year' statement; the suggestion that people who are not sure if they are eligible should apply anyway; the required-application-info list (full legal name and date of birth for at least one person applying, a mailing address for at least one person applying, and a signature); the documents table quoted in required_documents; the decision timeline (up to 45 days for DSS to decide, up to 90 days for disability applications); and the link to the DHB-5200 printable application PDF.

sources.title: DHB-5200 Application for Health Coverage (NC DHHS policies)
sources.supports: Claim-verification note (HACK-17): PDF retrieved 2026-10-30 from the printable-application link on medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/apply; form revision IA-9-2020 per the file name and the form footer. Verified on the form itself: the home-address field prints 'Leave blank if you don't have one' with a separate mailing-address field for people whose mail goes elsewhere, and Step 2 prints that family members who don't need health coverage do not have to provide immigration status or a Social Security Number. DHB-5200 vs DHB-5201 reconciliation: the official apply page presents DHB-5200 as the printable application for the household health-coverage journey and DHB-5201-ia as the 'short form' for a single adult with no dependents and no employer health coverage; the demo journey is the INITIAL MAGI Medicaid application for a household, so DHB-5200 governs. Handoff passages (HACK-46 and HACK-47), re-read 2026-10-31 on the committed copy of this retrieval (sha256-pinned in tests/test_forms_registry.py): page 1, under 'What happens next?', says to send the complete, signed application to the Department of Social Services in the county where you live, to sign and submit it anyway if you don't have all the information asked for, that they will follow up within 1-2 weeks with instructions on the next steps, and, if you don't hear back, to visit the state's local DSS web page or call the help line; page 1, under 'Getting help with this application', says to call or visit your local DSS office; every page prints a help line number at the bottom; page 20 (Step 5, Read & Sign) says the person who filled out Step 1 should sign, with Signature and Date (mm/dd/yyyy) lines, that a change in your information must be reported within 10 calendar days, that the application date is the date the county Department of Social Services receives it, and that you can appeal a decision you think is a mistake and find out how by contacting the Department of Social Services; page 21 (Step 6) says to take or mail the completed application to your local county Department of Social Services. The local DSS link the form prints (www.ncdhhs.gov/dss/local/) returned 404 on 2026-10-31, so no step links it. Held back from the steps until a current official page confirms them, because this revision dates from 2020: the 1-2 week follow-up, the help line number, the 10 calendar day change reporting, and the application date line. Left out on purpose: the page 20 line about requesting coverage for medical bills from up to three months before the application month, a rule printed on the 2020 revision that no current official page in this entry confirms.

sources.title: Mecklenburg County Department of Community Resources — Apply for Benefits
sources.supports: Claim-verification note (HACK-17): page retrieved 2026-10-30. Verified on this page: Mecklenburg County residents apply for Medicaid online through North Carolina ePASS (or Mecklenburg County All Access), return paper applications in person at the county Community Resource Centers (each with a 24-hour secure document drop-off box), fax applications to the county fax number published on the page, or apply by phone through the Economic Services Call Center. County channels may change — re-verify before relying on a specific address, fax number, or phone number.

items: NC Medicaid eligibility is decided by the Department of Social Services under the program's official rules — never by this app.
You can apply at any time of the year, per the official application guidance.
The official guidance says that if you are not sure whether you are eligible, they suggest you apply anyway.

This entry covers the initial Medicaid application for a household (the DHB-5200 health-coverage application). The DHB-5201 'short form' is the official alternative for a single adult with no dependents and no employer health coverage.
No income limits or eligibility thresholds are stated in this entry: the official eligibility guidance decides them, and the application form's examples are not treated as current limits.
Full legal name and date of birth for at least one person applying, and a mailing address for at least one person applying.
Your signature on the application — written, voice, or digital depending on how you apply.

If you have them, copies of documents for: North Carolina residency (a photo ID with your address, a utility bill, a lease or mortgage agreement, a vehicle registration, or employment documentation — or the application's 'NC Residency Declaration' box if you have no document).
Income documents if employed: pay stubs, employer verification, or your most recent tax return; if self-employed: your most recent tax return or copies of your business records.
Date of birth: a photo ID with your date of birth listed, or a birth certificate.
Social Security Number: a copy of your Social Security card or proof you applied for one, another official document with your name and SSN, or a military ID card.
Citizenship: a birth certificate or a passport. Immigration status for non-U.S. citizens: a copy of your visa/immigration card.
The official page says including copies of the documents you have may speed up the process, and that not all documents apply to everyone.

items.label: Apply online through ePASS (an NCID is required)
How to apply for NC Medicaid (official application guidance)
When to apply
items.due: Any time of the year — the official application guidance states you can apply at any time.

items.label: Decision timeline after you apply
items.due: The official page states it can take up to 45 days for the Department of Social Services to decide, and up to 90 days for disability applications — an agency processing timeline, not a promise about any case.

items.label: Make sure it has the basics
items.detail: The official guidance says an application must include a full legal name and date of birth for at least one person applying, a mailing address for at least one person applying, and a signature.

items.label: Sign and date it
items.detail: Step 5 of the form, on page 20, asks you to read the application and sign it, with a line for the date in mm/dd/yyyy format. The form says the person who filled out Step 1 should sign it.

items.label: Send it even if some answers are missing
items.detail: The form says that if you don't have all the information it asks for, you should sign it and send it in anyway.

items.label: Take it or mail it to your county DSS office
items.detail: Step 6 of the form, on page 21, says to take or mail your completed application to your local county Department of Social Services.

items.label: If you live in Mecklenburg County, you can drop it off or fax it
items.detail: Mecklenburg County's Apply for Benefits page says county residents can return a paper application in person at a Community Resource Center, where each center has a 24-hour secure drop-off box, or fax it to the county fax number published on that page. Check the page for the current locations and fax number before you go.

items.label: Or apply online through ePASS instead
items.detail: Instead of sending the paper form, you can apply online through ePASS, the state's online application. The official guidance says it needs an NCID, and the online application calls NC Medicaid "Medical Assistance".

items.label: Ask your county DSS office for help
items.detail: For help with the application, the form says to call or visit your local DSS office.

items.label: How long a decision can take
items.detail: The official guidance says it can take up to 45 days for the Department of Social Services to decide, and up to 90 days for disability applications. That is the agency's timeline, not a promise about any one case.

items.label: If you have questions or don't hear back
items.detail: The form says to call or visit your local DSS office for help with your application, including if you don't hear back after you send it.

items.label: If you think a decision is wrong
items.detail: The form says that if you think the agency made a mistake, you can appeal and ask for a fair review, and that you can find out how by contacting the Department of Social Services.

items: Pick a channel: apply online through ePASS, in person at your local Department of Social Services, over the phone, or by mail, email, fax, or drop-off.
If you apply on paper, download, print, and fill out the DHB-5200 application first.
Include copies of the documents you have — the official page says it may speed up the process.
Sign the application — the official guidance reminds applicants not to forget to sign.
After you apply, the agency may contact you for more information, so keep the address and phone number on the application correct.

items.reason: This entry describes North Carolina's state Medicaid program and its official application paths.
